question: Why is Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November?
notes: Narration v3. Times are seconds into voice.mp3, computed from words.json by shots.py. Each scene is one stop on the vertical paper strip. "paint" lists where the paint lands and the word it lands on.

scenes.line: Why is Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November? It used to be the last Thursday.

art.desc: A November wall calendar (a plain grid, 7 columns x 5 rows) above a roast turkey on a platter

scenes.line: Abraham Lincoln picked it, and later presidents usually kept it.

art.desc: Abraham Lincoln, from the side, writing with a quill

scenes.line: Then came 1939. That November had five Thursdays, so Thanksgiving would land on the very last day of the month.

art.desc: A November wall calendar (a plain grid, 7 columns x 5 rows) above a roast turkey on a platter
A 1930s shop window with toys and gifts; a worried shopkeeper beside it

paint.on: a gift box in the window

scenes.line: Back then, most people waited until after Thanksgiving to start their Christmas shopping.

art.desc: Shoppers in 1930s coats waiting at closed store doors with a wreath

scenes.line: A late Thanksgiving meant a short shopping season, in the middle of the Great Depression.

art.desc: An open, nearly empty wallet and two coins

scenes.line: So they asked President Franklin Roosevelt to move Thanksgiving up a week. He did.

art.desc: Franklin Roosevelt, from the side, at an old radio microphone

scenes.line: The country split. Some states followed him. Others kept the old date.

art.desc: A plain US map with state lines
An outline of Texas with two little roast turkeys in it
A frowning man in a 1930s hat pointing at a wall calendar

scenes.line: Families in neighboring states sat down to turkey a week apart.

art.desc: Two small houses with a signpost between them

scenes.line: Did the extra week help the stores? Roosevelt later admitted it didn't work. Most stores said it made little difference.
In 1941, Congress made it law: Thanksgiving is the fourth Thursday of November.
Most years, the fourth Thursday is also the last. But some Novembers have five.
